content:
Apple Pay is a must-have for iPhone users when shopping in physical stores, online shops, and apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more useful. Here's how they work.

iOS 27 new design

One of the changes I like most in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier to switch between cards during checkout on websites and apps.

Under the new design, you can easily swipe to switch between cards on the Apple Pay main checkout screen. You can also tap any card to see all available Apple Pay cards in a grid view.

The new design also makes it easier to see detailed information for each card, including rewards, balances, instalment options, and more.

iOS 27 is already available to developers and public beta testers, and will officially launch for all users this autumn.

Amex rewards points

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership programme that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When you shop online or in apps with your Amex card, you'll see a new "Use Rewards" option in the Apple Pay checkout flow, showing your available Membership Rewards points balance next to it. You can use points to pay for all or part of that purchase.

Amex points redeemed via Apple Pay are worth 0.7 US cents each. For example, 10,000 points can be converted into US$70 to offset your purchase amount.

Tap to Share

In iOS 27, Apple has added a new "Tap to Share" feature that works with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone, which Apple says will launch this autumn. Apple explains:

Customers can simply tap to connect with participating merchants' iPhones for a more personalised and faster in-store shopping experience, and safely share information such as email and other contact details, shipping addresses, membership rewards data, and more. Customers can also see in real time what's in their shopping basket, keep track of what they've bought, and make sure all offers and discounts are applied correctly.

When done, customers can complete checkout using Apple Pay on their iPhone.

Topping up debit cards

Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface.

According to Apple, you can top up supported debit cards directly through Apple Pay, either in Apple Wallet or at checkout.

Summary

As Apple Pay becomes more widely adopted among retailers, it's great to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. For me, whether shopping online or in person, Apple Pay is my go-to checkout payment method.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favourite Apple Pay features? Let us know in the comments.
